digest.top_line: POSEIDON IPD (n=6057): adding HT to postop RT misses OS (HR 0.87, 0.76-1.01, p=0.06); benefit concentrates at pre-RT PSA >0.5 (interaction p=0.02).
digest.tldr: Prostate carried the day, and both readings push RT decisions toward patient selection over blanket intensification: POSEIDON says HT with salvage RT earns its OS case only at higher pre-RT PSA (NNT 125 at ≤0.2 vs 25 at >1.0), while GÖTEBORG-1 shows 25yr PC-specific survival of 94% on AS against 68% failure-free at 22yr. Elsewhere the signal is planning-level: MIBC dose escalation cut invasive local recurrence (SHR 0.20) with no added G2+ toxicity, and immune-sparing lung SBRT spared 13.4% of ALC reduction.

sites.intro: First IROCK consensus contours for RCC SABR, with the least agreement on exactly the cases that need it most (IVC thrombus extent, ablation cavity).

studies.name: IROCK Contouring Guidelines
studies.tldr: First international consensus contouring guideline for RCC SABR; median DSC 0.85 across 4 cases, 16 radiation oncologists.
details: 🔍 Modified-Delphi style consensus: 16 rad oncs affiliated with IROCK contoured 4 scenarios, refined over 2 consensus meetings
🔍 Cases: >10cm tumor with IVC tumor thrombus; central tumor abutting hilum; post-nephrectomy local recurrence; ablation-cavity recurrence post-RFA
📐 Agreement analyzed by STAPLE (95% CI); median DSC 0.85, median MDA 2.17mm, median HD 9.00mm
📐 Median DSC >0.70 for every case (the paper's threshold for "good agreement")

subdetails: Case 1: include primary tumor + entire tumor thrombus; exclude bland thrombus
Case 2: include all tumor visible on sim imaging, account for internal motion
Case 3: include all visible gross tumor; surgical clips need not be included
Case 4: include visible gross recurrence + the entire ablation cavity

details: 📊 OAR dose constraints take priority over target volume coverage in planning
📊 Ipsilateral renal cortex = ipsilateral parenchyma minus iGTV, renal pelvis, renal vasculature, proximal ureter; hilum contour optional
🔍 Contrast-enhanced MRI and/or multiphasic contrast CT encouraged, with expert radiology review, to separate tumor from bland thrombus
⚠️ 2-way ANOVA: DSC and HD differed significantly by case but not by participant; MDA differed by both case and participant
⚠️ Greatest variation in Case 1 (superior extent of IVC thrombus, target size) and Case 4 (ablation cavity), so the hardest cases are the least standardized
⚠️ Renal cortex and renal hilum remain investigational substructures: neither has been separately correlated with renal-function outcomes
⚠️ Expert-opinion consensus, no outcome data; contour agreement is a surrogate, not local control or toxicity

verdict.rationale: Expert consensus contouring guideline, no outcome data. Standardizes an emerging practice rather than testing it; agreement metrics are process surrogates.
verdict.audience: Localized/recurrent RCC being planned for SABR (incl. IVC thrombus, post-RFA…

studies.significance: The high-variance cases are the actionable part: superior extent of IVC tumor thrombus (Case 1) and the post-RFA ablation cavity (Case 4) drove the spread even among IROCK experts, and consensus is to include both entirely in the iGTV. The renal cortex definition (kidney minus iGTV, pelvis, vasculature, proximal ureter) gives a reproducible denominator for renal-function constraints.
studies.monday_clinic: For a localized RCC pt being planned for SABR with IVC tumor thrombus or a recurrence in a prior RFA cavity, this supports carrying the full thrombus or cavity in the iGTV and letting OAR constraints outrank coverage; it does not inform dose, fractionation, or whether SABR beats nephrectomy.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: International expert consensus exercise under IROCK. **16 radiation oncologists** independently contoured 4 clinical scenarios plus 2 investigational renal substructures, with contours analyzed by **STAPLE (95% CI)** and statements refined over **2 consensus meetings**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Target scenarios: large (**>10 cm**) tumor with **IVC tumor thrombus**, central tumor abutting the renal hilum, post-nephrectomy local recurrence, and **ablation cavity recurrence after RFA**. Consensus: **any tumor thrombus or ablation cavity is included in the target volume**, bland thrombus is excluded, surgical clips can be excluded when uninvolved, and the iGTV must account for internal motion.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Contour agreement metrics rather than clinical outcomes: **dice similarity coefficient (DSC)**, Mean Distance to Agreement (MDA), and Hausdorff Distance (HD) per case.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Median **DSC 0.85**, median **MDA 2.17 mm**, median **HD 9.00 mm**. Median DSC was **>0.70 for every case**, the paper's bar for good agreement; 2-way ANOVA showed DSC and HD differed by case but not by participant.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents radiation oncologists planning SABR for localized or locally recurrent RCC, including IVC thrombus and post-ablation cavity targets. Does not represent metastatic RCC, dose/fractionation selection, or OAR constraint definitions beyond the renal cortex/hilum contours.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Agreement was weakest exactly where the guidance is most needed: **Case 1** (superior extent of IVC thrombus) and **Case 4** (ablation cavity) carried the largest MDA/HD spread. The renal cortex and hilum are labeled **investigational**, since neither substructure has been separately correlated with post-SABR renal function, so contouring them does not yet come with a constraint to meet.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The instruction to let **OAR constraints outrank target coverage** is the planning-philosophy statement here, and it differs from the coverage-first habit of most SABR sites. Combined with expert radiology review to separate tumor from bland thrombus, the guideline is mostly about avoiding the two errors that inflate a renal target: over-including thrombus and over-including cavity.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The variance concentrated in Case 1 (superior extent of IVC tumor thrombus) and Case 4 (post-RFA ablation cavity), and consensus includes both entirely in the iGTV. Renal cortex is defined as ipsilateral parenchyma minus iGTV, renal pelvis, vasculature, and proximal ureter, giving a reproducible denominator for renal-dose reporting.

open_questions: Does limiting renal hilum dose reduce adverse events?
Does renal cortex dose predict post-SABR renal function loss?
Do consensus contours improve local control or toxicity?

sites.intro: Retrospective TMT series putting a SIB boost to the primary tumour bed on the table for invasive local control, without a randomised comparator.

studies.name: Dose-Escalated RT for MIBC (TMT)
studies.tldr: SHR 0.20 (0.05-0.89) for invasive local recurrence with SIB dose escalation in TMT; no OS or MFS difference.
details: 📊 1° signal: invasive local control favored escalation, SHR 0.20 (0.05, 0.89), p=0.035, adjusted for T stage

details.text: 🔍 Multicentre retrospective, N=107, TMT with contemporary technique, 2015-2025, median f/u 23 mo
🔍 RT dose by cohort (SIB to primary lesion in the escalated arm)

details: 📊 Non-invasive local control p=0.8, MFS p=0.8, OS p=0.5: the benefit was confined to invasive recurrence
📐 No difference in G2+ GU (p=0.8) or G2+ GI (p=0.9) toxicity between cohorts
📊 No escalated pt required salvage cystectomy for invasive recurrence vs 2 standard-dose pts
🔗 Rationale is the mapping data cited by the authors: most invasive relapses arise near the original muscle-invasive tumour site
⚠️ Retrospective, non-randomised; escalation cohort selection (fitness, tumour visibility for GTV boost) is unmeasured confounding
⚠️ Wide CI (0.05-0.89) on few events; the point estimate of 0.20 is fragile

details.text: ⚠️ 23-mo median f/u is short for late GU toxicity after a bladder SIB, and effect sizes for the null endpoints are reported as p-values only in the abstract

verdict.rationale: Retrospective, N=107, single health-district cohorts; no randomised comparator and the invasive-LC estimate rests on few events. Authors themselves call for prospective study.
verdict.audience: MIBC undergoing trimodality therapy, fit for a boost-eligible GTV

studies.significance: The escalation was a simultaneous integrated boost to the primary lesion, not a whole-bladder dose lift, so the whole bladder stayed at 55Gy/20fx or 64Gy/32fx and G2+ GU/GI toxicity was unchanged (p=0.8, p=0.9). That is the parameter that makes this transferable: the decision it moves is whether to contour a GTV boost at TMT planning, and the benefit was specific to invasive recurrence (non-invasive LC p=0.8).
studies.monday_clinic: In MIBC pts proceeding to TMT with a resolvable primary GTV, this supports considering an SIB to the tumour bed within a standard whole-bladder schedule; it does not inform pts with non-invasive relapse risk alone, nor does it alter the cystectomy-vs-TMT choice.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Multicentre retrospective analysis** of MIBC pts treated with TMT using contemporary radiotherapy technique, **2015 to 2025**. **N=107**, median follow-up **23 months**. Sydney centres (Liverpool and Macarthur), ethics-approved, no external funding.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Standard cohort: **55Gy in 20 fractions** or **64Gy in 32 fractions** as a uniform dose to the whole bladder. Escalation cohort: a **simultaneous integrated boost** to the primary lesion, up to **60Gy in 20 fractions** or **70Gy in 32 fractions**, with the whole-bladder dose unchanged.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** 2-year local control, analysed separately for **invasive** and **non-invasive** disease. Secondary: metastasis-free survival, overall survival, bladder preservation, toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Dose escalation was associated with better invasive local control, **SHR 0.20 [0.05, 0.89], p = 0.035**, after adjusting for T stage. **No difference** in non-invasive local control (p=0.8), MFS (p=0.8) or OS (p=0.5).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Both cohorts tolerated RT well with **no difference in grade 2 or greater GU (p=0.8) or GI (p=0.9)** toxicity. No escalated pt required **salvage cystectomy** for invasive recurrence, versus two standard-dose pts.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents MIBC pts selected for trimodality therapy with a boostable primary tumour site. Does not represent pts going to upfront radical cystectomy, nor those treated with radiotherapy alone because chemotherapy was contraindicated.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Allocation to escalation was clinical, not randomised, so tumour visibility and pt fitness plausibly track with the boost. The invasive-LC confidence interval (0.05 to 0.89) rests on few events, and 23 months is short for late GU effects of a bladder boost.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The escalation was an SIB to the primary lesion, whole-bladder dose held at 55Gy/20fx or 64Gy/32fx, and G2+ GU/GI was unchanged (p=0.8, p=0.9). The decision it moves is whether to contour a GTV boost at TMT planning; the gain was confined to invasive recurrence, with non-invasive LC flat (p=0.8).
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Concurrent chemotherapy was the fixed backbone in both cohorts, so the invasive-LC signal (SHR 0.20) is attributable to the RT boost, not the regimen. For a med onc this argues for referring TMT candidates to a centre offering a boost rather than changing systemic choice, with MFS and OS unchanged (p=0.8, p=0.5).

open_questions: Does SIB dose escalation hold up in a prospective randomised TMT trial?
Late GU toxicity of a bladder boost beyond 2 years
Which pts have a GTV definable enough post-TURBT to boost?

sites.intro: Randomised phase II asking whether SBRT plan optimization around circulating-blood OARs preserves lymphocytes; surrogate endpoint only, and a preprint.

studies.name: Immune Cell Sparing RT
studies.tldr: ALC reduction improved 13.4% (95% CI 2.8-24.0, p=0.01) with immune-sparing SBRT planning vs standard, 29.5% in central tumors.
details: 📊 1° signal: ALC change from baseline at end-Tx / 4wk / 6mo, optimized -16%, -22%, -16% vs standard -31%, -34%, -26%
📐 Overall all-time-point improvement in ALC reduction 13.4 (5.3) %, 95% CI 2.8 to 24.0, p=0.01
📊 Central tumors carried the effect: optimized -8%, -18%, -14% vs standard -39%, -43%, -47%
📐 Central-tumor improvement 29.5 (9.6) %, 95% CI 10.1 to 48.9, p=0.004

details.text: 🔍 Phase II randomized, single-institution (UVA), 55 enrolled Feb 2020 to Apr 2023, 51 analyzed (25 optimized / 26 standard)

details: 🔍 Both arms met RTOG 0813/0915 dosimetric criteria; optimized plans additionally constrained heart, great vessels, thoracic spine, lymph-node stations
💊 G3 lymphopenia 15.4% standard vs 0% optimized; 2.8× more optimized pts had an ALC increase post-SBRT

details.text: 📐 Average % reduction, optimized vs standard plans (integral dose / V5 / V10)

details: ⚠️ Survival signals are underpowered and not significant: 2yr EFS 75.0% (SE 10.8) vs 59.8% (SE 11.2), p=0.10; 2yr OS 93.4% (SE 6.1) vs 69.4% (SE 10.5), p=0.14
⚠️ Those survival numbers are in treatment-naive pts only, and the arms were imbalanced: 88.5% treatment-naive standard vs 64.0% optimized, central tumors 36.0% optimized vs 23.1% standard
⚠️ medRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed; surrogate endpoint (ALC), no tumor-control or immune-function endpoint

verdict.rationale: Preprint, single-center randomized phase II, N=51, surrogate dosimetric/hematologic endpoint. Survival differences are non-significant and confounded by baseline imbalance in treatment-naive fraction.

studies.significance: The transferable part is the planning recipe: optimized plans hit RTOG 0813/0915 constraints while cutting V5 to thoracic spine 87%, vena cava 58%, heart 43%, so this is achievable on existing planning systems without dose compromise to the ITV (70-80 Gy to ≥70% of ITV in both arms). Central tumors, where blood and nodal stations sit in the low-dose bath, drove the effect (29.5%, p=0.004), so that is where adding immune-rich OARs to the optimizer is worth the planning time.
studies.monday_clinic: For an early-stage lung SBRT patient with a central tumor who is a candidate for subsequent immunotherapy, this supports adding heart, great vessels, spine and nodal stations as optimization structures when target coverage is unaffected; it does not extend to locally advanced NSCLC or conventionally fractionated thoracic RT, and it does not establish a survival benefit.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Randomized **phase II**, single institution (University of Virginia), accrual Feb 12 2020 to Apr 5 2023, database lock Jun 30 2024. **55 randomized, 4 withdrew/ineligible, 51 analyzed** (25 optimized, 26 standard). Interim toxicity analysis prespecified.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Early-stage lung cancer treated with SBRT**. Median age 74 in both arms (optimized range 56-90, standard 55-89). Baseline ALC 0.79 to 2.97 x10⁹ cells/L. Arms were imbalanced: **central tumors 36.0% optimized vs 23.1% standard**, treatment-naive **64.0% vs 88.5%**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Both arms met **RTOG 0813/0915** dosimetric criteria. The optimized arm additionally minimized dose to circulating blood and lymphatics: **heart, great vessels, lymph-node stations, thoracic spine**. Target coverage was preserved, with **70% or more of the ITV receiving 70-80 Gy** in the five illustrated cases.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary read is RIIS**, measured as absolute lymphocyte count change from baseline at end of treatment, 4 weeks and 6 months. Secondary: grade 3 lymphopenia, dose-volume correlates of RIIS, and exploratory EFS/OS.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Overall all-time-point improvement in ALC reduction **13.4 (5.3) %, 95% CI 2.8 to 24.0, p=0.01**; central tumors **29.5 (9.6) %, 95% CI 10.1 to 48.9, p=0.004**. Dose to heart, great vessels, thoracic spine and lymph nodes correlated significantly with RIIS.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **Grade 3 lymphopenia 15.4% in the standard arm, 0% in the optimized arm**. **2.8 times more** optimized pts had an ALC increase after SBRT. No added toxicity from the optimized planning is reported in the source.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents early-stage lung cancer treated with definitive SBRT, particularly central tumors near heart, great vessels, spine and nodal stations. Does not represent locally advanced NSCLC, conventionally fractionated thoracic RT, or pts receiving concurrent immunotherapy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Exploratory survival is in **treatment-naive pts only**, the subgroup where the arms differ most (88.5% vs 64.0%), so the 2yr OS gap (93.4% vs 69.4%, p=0.14) is not interpretable as an effect of planning. No immune-function or tumor-control endpoint links the ALC gain to outcome.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: This is the first randomized test of treating circulating blood and lymphatics as an OAR rather than modeling it retrospectively. It establishes that the constraint is achievable within existing protocol limits; whether preserved ALC converts to disease control, especially alongside immunotherapy, is untested here.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The planning recipe transfers: optimized plans met RTOG 0813/0915 while cutting V5 to thoracic spine 87%, vena cava 58% and heart 43%, with ≥70% of ITV still at 70-80 Gy. Central tumors drove the benefit (29.5%, p=0.004), so that is where adding immune-rich OARs to the optimizer earns its planning time.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Grade 3 lymphopenia was 15.4% standard vs 0% optimized, which matters most when SBRT precedes or accompanies checkpoint blockade, since post-RT ALC tracks with response. Nothing here establishes a disease-control benefit, so it does not change systemic selection or sequencing yet.

open_questions: Does preserved ALC translate into disease control or survival
Effect when SBRT is combined with checkpoint inhibition

sites.intro: Two long-horizon reads on when to treat and when to intensify: PSA-gated hormone therapy with postop RT, and 25-year outcomes of surveillance in a screened cohort.

studies.name: GÖTEBORG-1
studies.tldr: PC-specific survival 94% at 25yr on active surveillance, but failure-free survival fell to 68% at 22yr.

details.text: 🔍 Prospective AS cohort nested in the Göteborg-1 screening trial: 488 men, 1995-2014, follow-up closed Dec 31 2023
🔍 Risk mix: very-low-risk 251 (51%), low-risk 129 (26%), intermediate-risk 108 (22%); 6 high-risk excluded
🔍 Median age 66 (IQR 63-68), median PSA 4.1 ng/ml (IQR 3.4-5.4), median PSA density 0.12 (IQR 0.09-0.16)
🔍 Median follow-up 18.0 yr (IQR 14.7-22.1) among men alive at last follow-up
📊 Whole cohort at 22 yr: treatment-free survival 38%, failure-free survival 68%
📊 Outcomes by baseline risk group (KM estimates)
📊 232 men discontinued AS; definitive local therapy in 185

subdetails: PSA relapse after curative treatment, no hormones: 18

details.text: ⚠️ No predefined AS protocol; PSA q6-12mo and biopsy only on clinical progression signals
⚠️ Pre-MRI era: sextant biopsies until 2009, prediagnostic MRI in only 21 of 488 pts, so baseline risk was likely understaged
⚠️ Competing mortality dominates: 264 all-cause deaths vs 14 PC deaths, OS 32% at 25 yr for the whole cohort

details: 🔗 vs ProtecT, where AS carried a higher metastasis risk than immediate treatment; here failure accrued steadily rather than plateauing

verdict.rationale: Prospective single-strategy cohort, no randomised comparator to immediate treatment; risk stratification predates MRI and 12-core biopsy, limiting transfer to current AS entry criteria.
verdict.audience: Screen-detected very-low- to intermediate-risk prostate cancer, median age 66

studies.significance: The RT-relevant signal is when surveillance ends, not whether it is safe: 44 of 488 men reached radiotherapy and 18 had PSA relapse after curative treatment with no hormones, so salvage-eligible disease keeps arriving past 20 yr. Intermediate-risk failure-free survival was 55% at 19 yr vs 85% very-low-risk, the widest split in the dataset.
studies.monday_clinic: In screen-detected intermediate-risk disease considering surveillance, the 55% failure-free survival at 19 yr argues for counselling on decades-long monitoring rather than a discharge point; it does not speak to MRI-staged, targeted-biopsy cohorts entering AS today.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective observational cohort inside the **Göteborg-1** PSA screening trial. Of 1052 screen-detected cancers diagnosed 1995 to 2014, 494 (47%) had AS as primary strategy; **488** low- or intermediate-risk men analysed. Kaplan-Meier estimates for treatment-free, failure-free, PC-specific, and overall survival.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Very low risk (T1c, Gleason 6, PSA density <0.15, <3 positive cores) **251**, low risk **129**, intermediate risk (T1-2, Gleason ≤7, PSA <20 ng/ml) **108**. Median age **66 yr**, median PSA **4.1 ng/ml**. High-risk (Gleason ≥8) excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: PSA every **6-12 mo**, repeat biopsy only on signs of clinical progression (PSA and/or stage); early rebiopsy if <2 mm cancer on the diagnostic core. Treatment recommended on PSA, grade, or stage progression, or by patient preference.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: RT was the discontinuation route for **44 of 232** men leaving AS, versus 141 prostatectomy and 47 hormonal. Post-treatment **PSA relapse** was defined as ≥0.2 ng/ml after RP or nadir +2 ng/ml after radiation.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Treatment-free, failure-free, PC-specific, and overall survival from diagnosis. Failure counted PC death, metastasis, hormonal treatment, or PSA relapse after curative treatment. Curves truncated at 22 yr, and 24 yr / 19 yr in risk-stratified analyses.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: PC-specific survival **94% at 25 yr**; 14 PC deaths against 264 all-cause deaths. Treatment-free survival **38%** and failure-free survival **68%** at 22 yr; overall survival **32%** at 25 yr.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents screen-detected very-low- to intermediate-risk prostate cancer diagnosed by sextant or 12-core biopsy without MRI staging. Does not represent MRI-staged, targeted-biopsy AS cohorts or Gleason ≥8 disease, which was excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: No predefined surveillance protocol, so biopsy timing varied with individual urologist practice and failure detection is not standardised. Risk assignment used sextant biopsies before 2009 with prediagnostic MRI in only 21 men, so some intermediate-risk failures may be understaged high-risk disease enrolled at baseline.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Failure accrued without a plateau: **no safe window** for stopping surveillance emerges across 22 yr. With OS 32% at 25 yr against 94% PC-specific survival, competing mortality, not prostate cancer, decides most of these men's outcome.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Radiotherapy was the exit route for 44 of the 232 men who left AS, and 18 men had PSA relapse after curative treatment without hormones, so post-AS salvage-eligible disease keeps presenting past 20 yr. Intermediate-risk failure-free survival 55% at 19 yr vs 85% very-low-risk frames who arrives in an RT clinic later.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: 44 of 81 failures were hormonal treatment, the single largest failure category, well above the 14 PC deaths and 5 metastatic events. Systemic therapy, not cancer death, is the dominant downstream endpoint of surveillance, and it accrued steadily across two decades rather than clustering early.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Radical prostatectomy accounted for 141 of 232 AS discontinuations, the commonest exit. With treatment-free survival 38% at 22 yr and only 30% at 19 yr in intermediate-risk men, most surveillance patients eventually reach an operative decision, many at an older age than at diagnosis (median 66 at entry).

open_questions: Do MRI and targeted biopsy change these long-term AS failure rates?
Optimal surveillance intensity and stopping age given competing mortality
Whether intermediate-risk disease belongs on surveillance at all

studies.name: POSEIDON
studies.tldr: OS HR 0.87 (0.76-1.01), p=0.06 adding hormone therapy to postop RT; 0.7% absolute at 10y, PSA-dependent interaction p=0.02.
details: 📊 1° EP overall survival: HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.76-1.01), p=0.06, primary not met
📊 10y OS 84.3% with hormone therapy vs 83.6% RT alone, projected absolute 0.7%

verdict.rationale: IPD from six randomised phase 3 trials, prespecified OS primary, 9y follow-up; the null result diverges from routine short-term ADT alongside post-prostatectomy RT.
verdict.audience: Post-RP biochemical recurrence, pre-PORT PSA mostly ≤0.5 ng/mL, PET-negative

studies.significance: The decision that moves is hormone therapy omission with post-prostatectomy RT: NNT 125 at PSA ≤0.2 vs 25 at PSA >1.0 ng/mL, and the long-term CI clears 1.0 only above PSA 1.6. The 3.8% 10y MFS gain failed surrogacy for OS, so it can't carry ADT on its own.
studies.monday_clinic: In a man with PET-negative biochemical recurrence and pre-RT PSA of 0.5 ng/mL or less, this supports prostate-bed radiotherapy without hormone therapy; it does not extend to PET-positive recurrence or to PSA above 1.0 ng/mL.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **IPD meta-analysis** of six randomised phase 3 trials of postoperative radiotherapy with or without hormone therapy, N=**6057**, assembled through the MARCAP consortium (PROSPERO CRD42019134376). Pooled trials were RTOG 9601, GETUG-AFU-16, RADICALS (three trials) and RTOG 0534. Median follow-up **9.0 years** (IQR 7.2-10.7).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Recurrent prostate cancer after radical prostatectomy referred for PORT. Across the **5026** men randomised to radiotherapy with or without hormone therapy the median pre-PORT PSA was **0.3 ng/mL**; short-term stratum n=3938 (median PSA 0.3), long-term stratum n=1088 (median PSA 0.5).

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Hormone therapy was either **short-term, 4 to 6 months**, or **long-term, 24 months**, added to postoperative radiotherapy.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Target was the **prostate bed with or without pelvic lymph nodes**. Dose, fractionation and target-volume detail are **not reported in the source text** and differ across the six pooled trials, so transfer to a given technique cannot be read off this analysis.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: overall survival.** Metastasis-free survival was reported alongside it. Tests for interaction by pre-PORT PSA and by hormone therapy duration were prespecified, and non-linear associations between pre-PORT PSA and overall survival were modelled.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: No interaction by hormone therapy duration (p**interaction**=0.17), but a significant interaction with pre-PORT PSA above vs at or below 0.5 ng/mL (p**interaction**=0.02). Short-term hormone therapy showed **no OS or MFS benefit at any PSA below 2.4 ng/mL**; long-term hormone therapy above PSA 0.5 gave OS **HR 0.79, p=0.049**.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: No comparative toxicity data in the source. The authors set the null result against the known burden of hormone therapy on quality of life, cardiovascular, metabolic, musculoskeletal, sexual and neurocognitive function, and against **other-cause mortality offsetting cancer-specific benefit** in nonaggressive disease.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Of the pooled trials only **RTOG 9601** showed an OS benefit, and it was a late-salvage trial. A prior aggregate study-level meta-analysis of the same trials also found no OS benefit; what the IPD adds is the **pre-PORT PSA threshold** and the duration read.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PET-negative biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy with pre-PORT PSA at or below 0.5 ng/mL. Does not represent PET-positive nodal recurrence, or pts selected by Decipher or PSMA PET, both of which postdate this enrollment.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The long-term hormone therapy stratum is small (n=1088), so the PSA above 1.6 ng/mL signal rests on few pts, and the short vs long duration comparison was exploratory. Median pre-PORT PSA of 0.3 ng/mL means the higher-PSA strata driving the interaction are thinly populated.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: PORT itself is unchanged; what moves is whether hormone therapy rides along. At pre-RT PSA of 0.2 ng/mL or less the NNT is 125 against a 0.7% projected 10y absolute OS gain, and the long-term CI clears 1.0 only above PSA 1.6 ng/mL.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Duration is the systemic read: 24 months buys nothing over 4 to 6 months (exploratory HR 0.89, p=0.37) and there is no duration interaction (p=0.17). The 3.8% MFS gain failed surrogacy for OS, so hormone therapy toxicity trades against a non-surrogate endpoint. Biomarker selection (NRG-GU-006, BALANCE) is the open path.

papers.title: First Measurement: Proactive Immune Cell Sparing in Radiation Therapy
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Radiation Therapy (RT) can modulate the immune system and generate anti-tumor T cells. However, this anti-tumor-activity is countered by radiation-induced immunosuppression (RIIS). Clinical advantages of proactively sparing RT dose to immune rich organs have not previously been evaluated. Methods We conducted a phase II randomized trial from 2020 to 2023, enrolling 51 early-stage lung cancer patients treated with SBRT, to evaluate the effect of dose reduction to immune rich organs on RIIS. Two groups were: RIIS-optimized-treatment (lowering the dose to blood, bone-marrow and lymph-node-stations) and standard-treatment. All treatments followed national protocol guidelines. Peripheral blood was collected at baseline, immediately, 4-weeks and 6-months post-treatment. Results ALC changes from baseline immediately, 4-weeks and 6-months post-SBRT are: optimized-arm: -16%, -22%, -16%, standard-arm: -31%, -34%, -26%, leading to an overall-all-time-point improvement in ALC reduction in the optimized-arm compared to the standard-arm of 13.4 (5.3) % (95% CI, 2.8 to 24.0; p = 0.01). Central tumors had the largest improvement in ALC from baseline: optimized-arm: - 8%, -18%, -14%, standard-arm: -39%, -43%, -47%, leading to an overall-all-time-point improvement in ALC reduction in the optimized-arm compared to the standard-arm of 29.5 (9.6) % (95% CI, 10.1 to 48.9; p = 0.004). Grade 3 lymphopenia occurred in 15.4% of standard arm patients but was absent in the optimized arm. Additionally, 2.8 times more patients in the optimized arm experienced an ALC increase post-SBRT. Dose to organs such as the heart, great vessels, thoracic spine, and lymph nodes significantly correlated with RIIS. A trend towards increased Event-Free-Survival (two-year: 75.0% (SE = 10.8%) versus 59.8% (SE = 11.2%), p =0·10) and Overall Survival (two-year: 93.4% (SE=6.1%) versus 69.4% (SE=10.5%), p =0·14) was observed with optimized-planning compared to standard-planning in treatment naïve patients. Conclusion Reducing RT dose to immune rich organs significantly reduces RIIS compared to standard-of-care. This has implications in enhancing immune system mediated anti-tumor-activity. (Funded by National Cancer Institute and others. ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04273893 )
